title: Past Habits, Friendships and Storytelling
subtitle: A2+/B1 practice on used to, past stories, class reunions and friendship vocabulary.
lessonNotes: Use used to + base verb for a past habit or state that is no longer true.
For a past story, use Past Continuous for an action in progress and Past Simple for a shorter completed event.
Use in for months, years and longer periods; on for days and dates; at for exact times.
Build stories with first, then, afterwards and finally.

grammar.title: Used to: past habits and states
grammar.rule: Use used to + base verb for something that was true or regular in the past but is different now. In negatives and questions, use did not use to / Did ... use to?
examples: She did not use to like ice skating.
Did you use to meet classmates after school?

grammar.title: Past Simple and Past Continuous
grammar.rule: Use Past Continuous for background actions in progress. Use Past Simple for a shorter action that happened during or after them.
examples: I was walking home when I ran into a friend.
While they were talking, the bus arrived.
We met at a reunion last year.

grammar.title: Time and sequence
grammar.rule: Use in, on and at accurately, then connect events in a clear order.

vocabulary.meaning: a meeting of former classmates after a long time
vocabulary.example: They met again at a class reunion.

vocabulary.meaning: to leave school before completing a course
vocabulary.example: He did not drop out of school; he finished his course.

vocabulary.meaning: to stay away from school without permission
vocabulary.example: She never used to skip school.

vocabulary.meaning: to make people feel more comfortable when they first meet
vocabulary.example: A simple question can break the ice.
I ran into an old classmate at the station.
She told her friend the news in strict confidence.

vocabulary.meaning: to talk about a worry or feeling
vocabulary.example: Talking helped him get it off his chest.

practice.q: Choose the correct sentence about a changed past habit.
opt: I used to play chess after school.
I use to played chess after school.
I was use to play chess after school.
practice.a: I used to play chess after school.

opt: She did not used to enjoy coffee.
She did not use to enjoy coffee.
She did not use enjoyed coffee.
practice.a: She did not use to enjoy coffee.
practice.why: After did not, use the base form: use.

opt: While I walked, I was seeing my friend.
While I was walking, I ran into my friend.
While I was walk, I ran into my friend.
practice.a: While I was walking, I ran into my friend.
practice.why: The longer action is Past Continuous; the shorter event is Past Simple.

practice.q: What does break the ice mean?
opt: Make a first meeting feel easier
practice.a: Make a first meeting feel easier
practice.why: It means making people more comfortable when they first meet.

opt: Did you use to live here?
Did you used to live here?
Were you use to live here?
practice.a: Did you use to live here?
practice.why: Use did + base verb in questions.

reading.title: The Unexpected Class Reunion
reading.text:
When Maya was at school, she used to be quiet and spend most breaks reading. Her friend Lina was more sociable and always knew how to break the ice with new people. Although they had different personalities, they shared a genuine interest in travel and animals. After they left school, they lost contact for several years.

Last Saturday, Maya was waiting for a train when she ran into Lina. Lina invited her to a class reunion that evening. At first Maya was nervous, but she went. Former classmates told stories, laughed about school days and talked in strict confidence about old worries. Afterwards, Maya felt happier because she had finally got something off her chest: she missed having close friends.

questions.q: What did Maya use to do during breaks?
questions.why: The text says she spent most breaks reading.

questions.q: When did Maya run into Lina?
opt: While she was waiting for a train
questions.a: While she was waiting for a train
questions.why: This is the background action in the story.

questions.q: Why did Maya feel happier afterwards?
opt: She talked honestly about a worry
questions.a: She talked honestly about a worry
questions.why: She got something off her chest.
She could break the ice with new people.

listening.title: Meeting an Old Friend
listening.instructions: Listen twice. First, listen for the main story. Then listen again for the past forms and time expressions.
listening.script:
Sam: Did you go to the reunion last night?
Nora: Yes. I did not want to go at first because I used to be very shy at school.
Sam: What changed your mind?
Nora: I was walking home when I ran into my old friend Eva. She said, ‘I will go with you.’
Sam: Was it difficult to talk to people?
Nora: No. Eva broke the ice, and afterwards I spoke to many classmates.
Sam: Great. Are you going to meet them again?
Nora: Yes, we are going to have coffee on Saturday at 11.

questions.q: Why did Nora not want to go at first?
What was Nora doing when she met Eva?
questions.why: Use Past Continuous for the action in progress.
Eva makes an offer with will.

questions.q: When are they going to have coffee?

writing.prompt: Write 80–110 words about a fictional person who meets an old friend or goes to a class reunion. Use used to for one past habit or state, Past Continuous + Past Simple for one event, and at least three unit expressions. Add one time phrase with in, on or at, and finish with a future plan.
